title: handoff-protocols-checkpoints-for-cross-functional-rollouts-wip
content:
Purpose:
This is the working playbook for cross-functional handoffs, checkpoints, and data contracts used during feature rollouts (canary, staged, and A/B). The goal: reduce ambiguity between Product, Eng, SRE, Observability, and Customer Success during launches, cut mean time to recovery for regressions, and create repeatable evidence for go/no-go decisions.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to non-breaking product changes to the Console and Runtime routing layers, model variants and routing policies, and telemetry/experimentation flags.
- Not intended for major infra migrations (see infra migration runbook).
- Expectation: feature flag + canary route created before traffic ramp.

High-level lifecycle and checkpoints (quick):
1) Pre-launch (owner: Product) — deliverables: PRD stub, evaluation prompt set, risk classification, rollout template (this doc).
2) Dev & QA (owner: Eng) — unit tests, integration tests, smoke script checked into repo, load test results pasted into rollout ticket.
3) Canary (owner: Eng + SRE) — initial traffic slice, telemetry baseline comparisons, alert thresholds set in Grafana and pager-duty policies verified.
4) Observability signoff (owner: Observability) — dashboards validated, logging enrichment present, data contract confirmed.
5) Ops handoff (owner: Product) — customer success and support briefed, runbook links shared, rollback criteria endorsed.
6) Gradual ramp (owner: Product + Eng) — phased traffic increases, experiment analysis for A/B, final closeout and learnings doc.

Minimum pre-launch checklist (must be completed before canary):
- PRD short description + risk level (low/medium/high).
- Feature flag created and accessible via feature-flags service; flag naming convention: team.feature.shortdesc (e.g., console.model-routing-safeguard).
- Canary route: /v1/allocations/feature_flag_name or traffic-split via gateway with labels.
- Smoke tests: 5 discrete scripted queries covering success, edge-case, and error paths; stored in repo under /smoke/<feature>.
- Eval set: ~50 curated prompts saved as JSONL in experiments bucket (path appended to ticket).
- Backstop compatibility test: older model variants must return compat responses for top-3 flows.
- Data contract: list of telemetry events (names + fields) with types and sampling rate.

Canary configuration template (example):
- Initial slice: 0.5% of requests (routing by hashed user_id) for 2 hours
- Expand to 5% after 2 hours if all checks pass
- Next increase: 20% after 24 hours with merge hold for manual review
- Canary becomes baseline at >= 72 hours and 95th percentile latency within threshold
- Traffic allocation should prefer new users for A/B to reduce regression blast radius

Primary metrics to monitor (tiered):
- Safety/functional (must be green): logical correctness rate, hallucination regressions, test case pass rate on eval set (delta <= 1.5% absolute), rerank precision@10 delta <= 1%.
- Reliability (critical): 99th p50/p95/p99 latency for text-gen and embeddings, API error rate (5xx) delta <= 0.05% absolute, instance OOM or GPU restarts = 0.
- Cost signals (guardrail): tokens-per-request delta, GPU utilization variance, per-token cost uplift > 10% triggers review.
- User-impact signals: CC ticket volume, top customer sessions affected, session abandonment rate.

Concrete signal queries (copy-paste friendly):
- Latency p95 (text-gen): SELECT percentile(latency_ms, 95) FROM api_requests WHERE model IN ('nova-1', "variant-x") AND route = "/v1/generate" AND ts > now() - interval '2 hours'
- Eval regression check: compare eval-run/<ticket-id>/baseline.jsonl vs eval-run/<ticket-id>/current.jsonl using experiments/eval-compare tool (script path provided in linked artifacts).

Alerting and thresholds (config examples):
- page: infra-oncall if 5xx rate > 0.5% sustained for 5 minutes
- page: serving-oncall if p95 latency increases by > 30% vs baseline for 10 minutes
- slack-notify: #console-rollouts for non-critical deviations (auto-silenced during initial 15m after ramp step)

Rollback decision matrix (quick):
- Immediate rollback (automated) triggers: complete outage for canary slice, persistent >1% 5xx delta, repeated GPU OOM events.
- Manual rollback recommended: performance regressions exceeding defined latency or hallucination thresholds AND customer-facing errors in top-10 routes.
- Rollback owner: Engineering lead on-call for the feature. Execution steps: flip feature flag, route traffic to baseline variant, confirm metrics stabilization, communicate to stakeholders (template below).

Handoff templates (short):
- Handoff message to CS + Support (copy):
  Subject: [Rollout Handoff] <feature> — Canary started at <time>
  Body: Short summary, canary allocation and tracking dashboard link, rollback criteria, SE contacts, expected ramp plan.

- Post-rollout summary (copy):
  Title, timeframe, final traffic allocation, key metrics (safety, reliability, cost), top 3 lessons, follow-ups and owners.

Experiment (A/B) guardrails unique to LLM features:
- Randomization must be salted by user_id and session_id separately to avoid leak when users share traffic across devices.
- Treatment buckets should be exposed in telemetry with bucket_id and variant_metadata fields.
- Significance windows: use sequential testing with alpha correction (recommended: alpha=0.01) for high-impact safety metrics; for product metrics use alpha=0.05 but require 2x consistency checks.
- Run minimum 7 full days for metrics that have weekly cycles, unless signal is overwhelmingly strong.
- For quality metrics evaluated by human raters, require at least 200 rated examples per variant before making roll decisions.

Observability and data contract checklist (for Observability signoff):
- Event schema: api_request.{start,complete}, generation.result, embed.request, rerank.request with explicit fields: model, variant, route, request_id, user_id_hash, bucket_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, error_code.
- Sampling: up to 100% for canary slice; 5% sampling for baseline by default.
- Log enrichment: injection of rollout_id and git_sha into every request log.
- Dashboards: canary overview (top-level), per-model quality, cost cadence, customer impact.

Human evaluation plan (if applicable):
- Create human eval rubric with explicit pass/fail criteria (safety, relevance, factuality, style).
- Raters: 3 independent raters per example; tie-break via majority.
- Gold set: include 10 known-edge cases to ensure rater attention.

Communication matrix (who to ping and when):
- First response (15m): feature owner + eng on-call + observability + PM.
- Escalation (1 hour): Eng manager + SLA lead + CS director.
- Customer notification (post stabilization or immediate if customer facing): Customer Success lead drafts message.

Open questions / TODOs (working):
- Should we make canary sampling salted by request fingerprint instead of user_id for ephemeral mobile sessions? Pros/cons: reduces reassign, increases representativity for anonymous traffic.
- Define standard cost-threshold formula: absolute vs relative on token cost? (impl note: use relative > 10% AND absolute > $0.001 per request to avoid noise).
- Auto-rollback integration: level of trust in automated rollback; proposal: automated only for hard infra signals, not for nuanced quality regressions.

Quick checklist for closing a rollout:
- Final metrics snapshot attached to ticket (CSV)
- Lessons learned doc + <owner> assigned
- Feature flag plan for long-term (kill date or migration plan)
- Retrospective with CS and SRE within 7 days

Notes to self / rough fragments (ok to be messy):
- consider adding a small "canary health score" composite: weighted sum of safety (50%), reliability (30%), cost (10%), user-impact (10%). Threshold > .85 for ramp.
- how to version eval sets cleanly? maybe experiments repo has dataset registry with tags. add a job that runs evals nightly for active rollouts.
- remind: update SDK docs for feature flag client with new sampling options.

References and quick links (for ticket):
- Rollout registry (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Rollout+Handoff+Registry
- Canary automation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1023
- Experiment analysis notebook template: experiments/notebooks/ab-analysis-template.ipynb

If you're reviewing: leave comments inline, tag @Sofia for data-contract questions and @Liam for automation/ops notes.

Unresolved: which SRE rotation owns post-roll stability checks when multiple features are ramping? (propose: dedicated rollout-oncall rotation that SRE can staff 09-17 M-F).

END OF DRAFT
